newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall 1.7 pct on oil price hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall 1.7 pct on oil price hike fears.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi bourse increased losses in afternoon trade on Wednesday as both local and foreign investors sold stocks on expectations of an oil price hike, brokers said.
At 12.45 p.m. (0715 GMT), the Delhi sensitive index was down 12.80 points, or 1.7 percent, at 753.12.
"Selling by foreign and domestic investors brought nervousness among players who also indulged in panic selling," said Bharat Bhushan Aggarwal of brokers Nu-Era Security.
The government is under pressure to find a way of paying off its mounting oil pool deficit -- money owed oil companies for selling products below market prices to subsidise consumers.
Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu said on Tuesday that the prime concern of the ministry is to contain the deficit but his ministry was not interested in hiking oil prices.
Reliance Industries lost five rupees at 288.
State Bank of India quoted 5.95 rupees lower at 297.
Larsen and Toubro lost 2.35 rupees at 208.
